issue: त्रैल तेश है नाम तुम्हारा — a name of Bhairava, printed as two words in the book; Drik Panchang (and Bhakti Bharat) print त्रैलतेश, Shubh Panchang बैलकतेश. None is a known name; the intended form (perhaps त्रैलोकेश, lord of the three worlds) is not settled.
our reading: त्रैल तेश, as the book prints it: a name of Bhairava (lord of the three worlds?).
alternatives: त्रैलतेश (one word); बैलकतेश; a corruption of त्रैलोकेश.

issue: गायत्री कहैं: who calls him Nimiṣa and Digambara — the goddess Gāyatrī, or his Gāyatrī mantra.
our reading: Gāyatrī calls you Nimiṣa and Digambara.

issue: आपहि वारे छीजन धाये: the opening of the Ailādī story; आपहि वारे and छीजन (a place?) are not settled, nor who ran where.
our reading: You yourself hastened away to Chījana, and Ailādī wept.
alternatives: 'Your own people (आपहि वारे) ran to Chījana'; छीजन not a place ('wasting away').

issue: गये हिवारे मैं तुम जाकर: Hivārā as a village (Ailādī's?), and whether Bhairava went there to her or away from her.
alternatives: Hivārā is Ailādī's village and he went there to her.

issue: प्रभु ने तुमको तुरत पठाया: which Lord sent Bhairava, Śiva (whose throne shook, cau35) or Viṣṇu (who speaks in cau37).
our reading: 'the Lord', unnamed, as the verse has it.
